name: git-poison
description: A VS Code extension that blocks a git commit of any file containing a "Poison Pill" string. Placing a pill stops accidental committing of unfinished TODOs, debug statements, secrets, etc. Also provides navigation to pill locations.

commands.title: Git Poison: Jump To Previous Poison Pill
Git Poison: Jump To Next Poison Pill

git-poison.overrideSecs.title: Override Blocking Timeout (Seconds)
git-poison.overrideSecs.description: Number of seconds that the override blocking command can be used. After this time, the commit blocking will be re-enabled.

git-poison.poisonPillString.title: Poison Pill String
git-poison.poisonPillString.description: The string used to indicate a poison pill in the code. This will be inserted by the "Insert Pill" command and be used to detect pills. Warning: If you don't remove old pills before changing this setting, you may accidentally commit them.

scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run lint
scripts.lint:watch: echo 'eslint:watch not used , running eslint extension instead'
